questions.prompt: Multiplicative uncertainty describes the plant error by bounding
questions.explanation: A multiplicative weight says \(|P - P_0| \le |W_m|\,|P_0|\), which is a relative bound. The absolute error is the additive weight \(W_a\). Sensitivity is a closed-loop map, not a description of the plant error. Bandwidth is a performance number.
questions.figure_alt: A bound that grows as frequency increases.

questions.prompt: The nominal gain is \(P_0 = 10\) and the true gain is \(P = 12\). The relative error \(|P-P_0|/|P_0|\) is
questions.explanation: \(|12-10|/10 = 0.2\). The absolute error is 2, which is the additive mismatch, not the relative one. The ratio \(12/10 = 1.2\) is the gain ratio, one plus the relative error.

questions.prompt: The nominal gain is 4 and the additive bound is \(|P - P_0| \le 0.5\). The largest possible \(|P|\) in that bound is
questions.explanation: The plant can sit 0.5 above the nominal, so the largest magnitude in the bound is \(4 + 0.5 = 4.5\). The nominal 4 leaves the whole uncertainty budget unused. Twice the bound, 1, is not a plant gain.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 234 120" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>nominal plant</title><text x="24" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">in</text><line x1="42" y1="56" x2="78" y2="56"/><polygon points="78,56 71.6,58.7 71.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="78" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="120" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">P0</text><line x1="162" y1="56" x2="198" y2="56"/><polygon points="198,56 191.6,58.7 191.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="202" y="60" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">out</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A single block for the nominal plant.

questions.prompt: A gain is known to within \(\pm 35\) percent. The multiplicative weight \(|W_m|\) that covers that range is
questions.explanation: A \(\pm 35\) percent gain error is exactly \(|W_m| = 0.35\). The factor 1.35 is the largest gain ratio \(P/P_0\), which is \(1 + W_m\), not the weight. Half of 35 percent would be a one-sided reading of a two-sided statement.
questions.figure_alt: A bound that grows as frequency increases.

questions.prompt: A resonant mode that was left out of the model is usually drawn as
questions.explanation: An unmodeled resonance is dynamics, and it shows up over a band of frequencies, so \(|W|\) is larger there. A constant interval on the DC gain is parametric uncertainty and does not capture a peak at one frequency. The reference is a command, not a plant error. Sensor noise is a different input to the loop.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 340 186" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a weight that grows with frequency</title><line x1="54" y1="140" x2="300" y2="140"/><polygon points="300,140 293.6,142.7 293.6,137.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="54" y1="140" x2="54" y2="28"/><polygon points="54,28 56.7,34.4 51.3,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="58" y="24" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">dB</text><polyline points="71,129.2 81.1,114.1 124.3,84 283,38.8" stroke-width="2.2"/><text x="300" y="156" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">f</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A magnitude that rises toward high frequency.
options: a constant parametric interval on the DC gain
dynamic uncertainty whose weight grows where the missing mode can be large
sensor noise, which is an external input rather than a plant error

questions.prompt: The nominal gain is 8 and the additive weight is \(|W_a| = 2.4\). The equivalent relative weight \(|W_a|/|P_0|\) is
questions.explanation: Dividing the additive bound by the nominal gain gives \(2.4/8 = 0.3\). The additive number 2.4 stays absolute until it is divided by \(P_0\). The sum \(8 + 2.4 = 10.4\) is the largest plant gain, not the relative weight.

questions.prompt: A resistor that lies somewhere in a known interval, with no extra dynamics, is
questions.explanation: One real parameter in an interval is the definition of parametric uncertainty. Unmodeled dynamics are extra states or extra modes, not a number in a range. A multiplicative weight may be used to cover the interval, but it does not have to grow with frequency if the error is a pure gain. A right-half-plane zero is a feature of the nominal model, not of an interval.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 234 120" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>nominal plant</title><text x="24" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">in</text><line x1="42" y1="56" x2="78" y2="56"/><polygon points="78,56 71.6,58.7 71.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="78" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="120" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">P0</text><line x1="162" y1="56" x2="198" y2="56"/><polygon points="198,56 191.6,58.7 191.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="202" y="60" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">out</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A single block for the nominal plant.
options: multiplicative uncertainty that must grow with frequency

questions.prompt: The nominal gain is 5 and a measurement of the plant gives 6.5. The absolute error \(|P - P_0|\) is
questions.explanation: \(|6.5 - 5| = 1.5\). The relative error is \(1.5/5 = 0.3\), which divides by the nominal gain. The measured value 6.5 is the plant, not the error.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 234 120" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>nominal plant</title><text x="24" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">in</text><line x1="42" y1="56" x2="78" y2="56"/><polygon points="78,56 71.6,58.7 71.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="78" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="120" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">P0</text><line x1="162" y1="56" x2="198" y2="56"/><polygon points="198,56 191.6,58.7 191.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="202" y="60" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">out</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A single block for the nominal plant.

questions.prompt: The nominal gain is 8 and \(|W_m| = 0.25\). The largest plant gain allowed by that multiplicative bound is
questions.explanation: \(P\) can be as large as \(P_0(1 + |W_m|) = 8\cdot 1.25 = 10\). The weight 0.25 is the relative budget, not a gain. The nominal 8 ignores the budget.
questions.figure_alt: A bound that grows as frequency increases.

questions.prompt: A multiplicative weight has \(|W_m| = 0.4\). The small-gain test \(|T W_m| < 1\) allows \(|T|\) up to
questions.explanation: The product bound rearranges to \(|T| < 1/|W_m| = 1/0.4 = 2.5\). The weight 0.4 itself is not a limit on \(T\). Twice the reciprocal, 5, doubles the room the test actually gives.

questions.figure_alt: A magnitude that rises toward high frequency.

questions.prompt: Making an uncertainty weight larger than the error you can actually justify
questions.explanation: A larger weight covers more plants, including ones outside the evidence. A controller that works for all of them is harder to find, not easier. The weight is part of the model. Shrinking the set would mean a smaller weight.
questions.figure_alt: A bound that grows as frequency increases.
options: makes every spec easier to meet
does not change the controller, because weights are not part of the model
shrinks the set of plants under consideration
is conservative: the spec is asked to hold for plants you do not believe are real

questions.prompt: The nominal gain is 20 and the multiplicative uncertainty is 30 percent. The largest plant gain in that bound is
questions.explanation: \(P \le 20\cdot 1.30 = 26\). Thirty percent of 20 is 6, which is the additive half-width, not the largest gain. The nominal 20 leaves the uncertainty out.
